audit.whatIsWrong: Every reference to the reflect treats it as an ultimate — 'her reflect is her ultimate, so it's nowhere near up to punish you', 'while her reflect ultimate is unavailable', 'after her R reflect is on cooldown'. No cooldown is given anywhere.
audit.why: Rebuttal is her W on 38/35/33/29/26 seconds. Treating it as an ultimate tells the reader it is rarely available when in fact it is up for most trades, and by rank 5 it is free (0 mana). Meanwhile Golden Eclipse, the actual ultimate, is 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal's 26-38s written into whys[1], spikes[0].text and early; Golden Eclipse's 120s into late.

audit.whatIsWrong: The ability slots are wrong across the whole page. The reflect is called R in six fields when it is W (Rebuttal). The execute is called E in two fields when it is the passive (Searing Brilliance / Overwhelm); E is Solar Snare, the root. 'Her zone (W)' is also wrong — W is the barrier; the zones are Radiant Volley (Q) and Solar Snare (E). And whys[4] asserts 'She has no level-6 kill spike — her R is a defensive reflect'.
audit.why: Golden Eclipse strikes every enemy marked with Overwhelm regardless of distance, dealing more per stack — it is a global kill threat, and calling it defensive tells the reader to ignore the one ability that can finish them from across the map after a lane's worth of poke. The reflect being her W rather than her R also inverts the trading rule: it is a routine cooldown to bait, not a rare ultimate. Since Rebuttal reflects projectiles and Gnar's Boomerang, Boulder Toss and GNAR! are ALL flagged projectiles, baiting it is the precondition for every committal Gnar has. Finally, per the mirror audit, Wallop is the unconditional 7s stun and GNAR! only stuns against terrain — spikes[1].text implied the fling itself was the stun.
audit.corrected: Reflect re-slotted to W (Rebuttal) in whys[0], whys[1], whys[6], spikes[0].text, spikes[1].text, early, late, wants.you[0], wants.you[2], wants.foe[1]; execute re-slotted to the Overwhelm passive in whys[6], spikes[3].text, wants.foe[2]; Golden Eclipse restated as a global threat in whys[4], mid and late; the Wallop-vs-wall distinction written into spikes[1].text and mid.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Mel carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items in and Mel takes over: stacked Overwhelm and a global ult. Carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides.

edits.before: Your ranged Mini autos plus a single Boomerang win the first trade against an immobile mage who only has Q to poke back and no reflect up yet.
edits.after: Your ranged Mini autos plus a single Boomerang win the first trade against an immobile mage with only Radiant Volley and no Rebuttal yet.

edits.before: Hyper's third-hit proc plus Boomerang lands a free chunk while her reflect ultimate is unavailable — your strongest early window.
edits.after: Hyper's third-hit proc plus Boomerang lands a free chunk before Rebuttal is ranked — the reflect is her W, not her ult, so it comes early.

edits.before: She has no level-6 kill spike — her R is a defensive reflect — so with Mega up you wall-combo a squishy mage for the kill.
edits.after: Golden Eclipse hits you at any range for every Overwhelm stack she has built — her R is a kill threat, not a defensive tool.

edits.before: Mel out-scales: her execute (E) and reflect (R) grow stronger in teamfights while your form-dependent burst plateaus at two-plus items.
edits.after: Mel out-scales: Overwhelm's stacking execute and Rebuttal's reflect grow in teamfights while your form-dependent burst plateaus at two items.

edits.before: Hyper's third-hit move-speed proc plus a Boomerang lands a chunky free trade — Mel's reflect is her ultimate, so it's nowhere near up to punish you. First hard punish window.
edits.after: Hyper's third-hit move-speed proc plus a Boomerang lands a chunky free trade — Rebuttal is her W at 38 seconds rank 1, so take the trade inside that gap. First hard punish window.

edits.before: Catch her in Mega: Wallop stuns or GNAR! flings her into the side wall for the wall-combo bonus stun and burst — a dashless squishy mage just dies. Her R reflect can't save her once she's airborne.
edits.after: Catch her in Mega: Wallop is the unconditional stun, and GNAR! only stuns if she hits a wall — a dashless squishy mage dies to that pair. Rebuttal reflects projectiles, so it eats a Boulder or GNAR!, never the Wallop.

edits.before: Past two items Mel's execute and reflect-R scale into teamfights while your form-dependent burst plateaus — close the lane and play front-to-back before her grouped damage outgrows your kiting.
edits.after: Past two items stacked Overwhelm and a global Golden Eclipse scale into teamfights while your form-dependent burst plateaus — close the lane and play front-to-back before her range outgrows your kiting.

edits.before: Mel is a squishy, immobile poke mage with no dash, so your Mini form bullies her once you hit level 2. Land the third Hyper hit for the move-speed proc and tag her with Boomerang — her only reflect is her ultimate (R), which she doesn't have early, so these trades are clean. Her Q out-ranges your Boomerang, so when your Rage is on cooldown and you're stuck in fragile Mini form, back off and farm rather than eating free poke. Don't dump a fat Boulder Toss or a Mega all-in into her once R is up — her reflect bounces it back — but with it down, step up and out-DPS her with sustained autos.
edits.after: Mel is a squishy, immobile poke mage with no dash, so your Mini form bullies her once you hit level 2. Land the third Hyper hit for the move-speed proc and tag her with Boomerang. Radiant Volley out-ranges your Boomerang, so when Rage is on cooldown and you're stuck in fragile Mini, back off and farm rather than eating free poke. The rule that matters: Rebuttal is her W, not her ult, and at 26-38 seconds it is available for far more trades than an ultimate would be — it reflects projectiles, so Boomerang, Boulder Toss and GNAR! all come back at you. Bait it, then commit.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 hinge entirely on whether Mega is up — that's the only variable that matters in this lane, since Mel has no real power spike at 6 (her ult is a defensive reflect, not a kill threat). With Mega form, walk in, Wallop to stun, and if there's a side wall near her, GNAR! flings her into it for a second stun and a huge chunk of her HP bar; a dashless mage has no way out of that combo. Without Mega, don't dive her in Mini with Rage down — her Q poke and zone (W) will punish you. Every Mega window where her R is down is a kill threat.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 hinge on whether Mega is up, but stop treating her 6 as harmless: Golden Eclipse is global and strikes you for every Overwhelm stack you are carrying, so the poke you have been eating is stored damage waiting to be cashed. With Mega form, walk in and Wallop to stun — that stun is unconditional — and if a side wall is near her, GNAR! flings her into it for a second stun; away from terrain GNAR! only displaces. Without Mega, don't dive her in Mini with Rage down: Radiant Volley and Solar Snare's root punish it.

edits.before: You still win the straight 1v1 if you can land a wall-combo, and your GNAR! is a far better teamfight tool than her reflect ult. But Mel scales: her execute (E) and her damage-reflect R get scarier in grouped fights, and at two-plus items your form-dependent burst plateaus while she farms range and AP from the backline. Close this lane and snowball a mid-game lead — play front-to-back, peel with GNAR!, and don't try to solo-kite her once her items come online. Win it before late and her scaling never gets to matter; let it go long and her reflect punishes your every committal.
edits.after: You still win the straight 1v1 if you can land a wall-combo, and your GNAR! is a far better teamfight tool than anything she brings to a brawl. But Mel scales: Overwhelm stacks without limit and Golden Eclipse cashes them from anywhere on the map every 120 seconds, and at two-plus items your form-dependent burst plateaus while she farms range and AP from the backline. Close this lane and snowball a mid-game lead — play front-to-back, peel with GNAR!, and remember Rebuttal reflects every projectile you own, so bait the barrier before you spend one.

notes: Mel's ability slots were wrong across the entire page. The reflect (Rebuttal) is her W on a 26-38 second cooldown, not her ultimate — the page said 'her reflect is her ultimate, so it's nowhere near up to punish you', which is the opposite of the truth and would get a reader's Boulder Toss bounced repeatedly. The execute is the passive (Overwhelm), not E; E is Solar Snare, the root. And whys[4] told the reader Mel has no level-6 kill spike because 'her R is a defensive reflect' — Golden Eclipse is a global that strikes every Overwhelm-marked enemy for damage per stack, so it is precisely a kill threat, and it converts a lane's worth of accumulated poke into a finish from off-screen. Worth flagging for a manual pass: the full layer's tracking frame is entirely 'Solar Snare' (focus.text, loading, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], report[5]/[9]/[10]/[13]); the cooldowns that actually gate Gnar's commits here are Rebuttal (the reflect) and Golden Eclipse. focus.text is 'Mel Solar Snare' at 15 characters, under the applier's 25-char skip threshold, so it cannot be fixed by an edit.
